Step 2 / 6 · Tell apart

Pairs that look alike

Passive → active⏱ 15 min
GoalTell apart sportspeople words and -ing patterns that are easy to mix up, and explain your choice.
2a
Compare the pairs
8′

Read both sides of each card, then cover them and try the quick test.

like doing · would like to do
like + ‑ing /laɪk/
a general taste or habit: something you do because it’s fun
I like swimming in the sea whenever I go home to Đà Nẵng.
would like + to /wʊd ˈlaɪk tə/
you want it, now or in the future (a wish or an offer)
I’d like to learn to sail before I turn thirty.
✗ My brother would like playing for a professional club one day. (→ to play)
an athlete · athletics
an athlete /ən ˈæθliːt/
a person who runs, jumps or throws in competitions
The athletes walked out into the stadium behind their national flags.
athletics /æθˈletɪks/
the sport itself: running, jumping and throwing events
Athletics was my favourite part of PE at secondary school.
✗ My cousin does athlete three times a week at the stadium. (→ athletics)
‑er · ‑ist · player
‑er /ə(r)/
football → a footballer, golf → a golfer, swim → a swimmer, box → a boxer
The swimmers stood on the blocks and waited for the beep.
‑ist /ɪst/
cycle → a cyclist, motorcycle → a motorcyclist
The cyclists came round the last bend in a tight group, all fighting for the line.
… player /ˈpleɪə(r)/
tennis → a tennis player, chess → a chess player, baseball → a baseball player
Most chess players at the club are students, but the best one is a retired surgeon.
✗ My cousin wants to be a professional cycler one day. (→ cyclist)
lose · loose
lose /luːz/
verb: not win; the ‑ing form is losing, with one o
We hate losing to the team from the floor below.
loose /luːs/
adjective: not tight, not fixed
My shoelace came loose halfway through the race, and I nearly fell.
✗ I was so tired of loosing that I almost quit the team. (→ losing)
sport · sporty
sport /spɔːt/
noun: football, swimming, judo and so on
Judo is a sport that teaches you how to fall safely.
sporty /ˈspɔːti/
adjective: a person who likes sport and is good at it
My younger brother is really sporty; he plays three different sports at school.
✗ My mother isn’t very sport, but she walks every evening. (→ sporty)
play · do · go
play /pleɪ/
ball games and games against someone: play football, play chess, play badminton
We play basketball on the court behind the canteen every Friday.
do /duː/
martial arts and activities without a ball: do judo, do karate, do yoga, do athletics
My roommate does judo, so nobody tries to wake him up suddenly.
go /ɡəʊ/
activities ending in ‑ing: go swimming, go running, go cycling
On Sunday mornings we go running round West Lake.
✗ Last year I played karate at a club near my house. (→ did)
bored · boring
bored /bɔːd/
how a person feels; be bored with + ‑ing
By the third hour of the cricket match, I was bored with watching and went for a walk.
boring /ˈbɔːrɪŋ/
what the thing is like: it makes people feel bored
A goalless draw with no shots on target is the most boring thing in sport.
✗ I’m boring with running round the same track every morning. (→ bored)
good at · good for
good at /ˈɡʊd ət/
you can do it well (+ a noun or a verb in ‑ing)
Hà is good at reading the game, so she always seems to be in the right place.
good for /ˈɡʊd fə(r)/
it helps you or does you good
Skipping is good for your footwork, which is why boxers do so much of it.
✗ Cycling to class is good at your heart and your legs. (→ good for)
2b
Which one, and why?
7′
1 · Would you like ____ in our basketball team on Saturday? We’re one player short.
to play: would like is a wish, so to + verb.
2 · A ____ needs strong legs and a light bike to get up a mountain road.
cyclist: the person takes ‑ist. Cycling is the sport, and cycler is not used.
3 · I hate ____ on penalties; it feels like bad luck, not a fair result.
losing: hate + ‑ing, spelt with one o. Loose means “not tight”.
4 · By the end of the second hour, the coach was ____ with watching the same mistakes.
bored: how the coach felt, in the pattern bored with + ‑ing.
5 · A banana half an hour before a long run is ____ your energy levels.
good for: the banana helps your energy. Good at is about a skill.
6 · My mother ____ yoga in the park every morning before work.
does: no ball and no ‑ing, so do (do yoga, do judo).
7 · The heptathlon is a two-day event in ____.
athletics: the name of the sport. An athlete is a person, and athletic is an adjective.
8 · My grandfather is still very ____ at seventy; he swims every morning.
sporty: an adjective after very. Sport is a noun.

How I stopped being a sore loser

At secondary school I was the worst kind of sore (1) a person, so the noun loser: a sore loser gets angry after a defeat. I hated (2) hate + ‑ing: hated losing so much that I once threw my racket into a hedge after a badminton match against my best friend. My coach didn’t shout. She just said, ‘(3) an activity as the subject: Winning feels great for a day, but you learn far more from the days you lose.’ After that, I got much better at (4) after the preposition at: shaking hands with a real smile, even after a painful defeat. I’m still very (5) an adjective after very: competitive, of course, and I’ll never enjoy a defeat. These days, though, I’m more afraid of (6) after the preposition of: playing badly than of losing, and I think that’s a healthier way to feel about sport.

Speaking task · a 20-second answer

‘Is winning important to you?’

Speak for about 20 seconds with Tier 1 words, using love, hate, be afraid of or be good at + ‑ing.

Example

Honestly, more than I’d like to admit. I love winning, whether it’s a 5 km run or a quiz in the common room, and I hate finishing near the bottom of any list. I’m not exactly good at hiding it either, so my friends tease me when I go quiet. I’m trying to care less about the score and more about playing well.

Now go through the 7-step frame and add two Tier 2 chunks, one short sentence per step.

Example

PointWinning still matters to me, but not as much as it did when I was fifteen. WhyBack then I thought a defeat made me a weaker person, not just a weaker player. HowNow I try hard in every game and let the result look after itself. ExampleIn March our platoon’s basketball team lost the league final by twenty points, mostly because nobody talked on the court. ResultInstead of blaming each other, we now start every practice with a drill where you shout a teammate’s name before you pass, and we finally sound like a team. LimitationI’d be lying if I said defeat doesn’t hurt at all; I still can’t stand losing a game we should have won. EvaluationStill, learning to lose well has probably taught me more than all my easy wins put together.

Choose a follow-up question and give a 20-second answer.

  • Is it ever OK to celebrate loudly in front of the team you’ve just beaten?
  • Which matters more in a team: one star player or good teamwork?
Example

Good teamwork, nearly every time. A star can win you one match, but a side that talks, passes and covers for each other wins the whole season.

Read the model and spot all seven steps.

PointWinning is important to me, but I’ve learned that it isn’t the only thing that counts. WhyThe reason is simple: I’m naturally competitive, and I’ve always loved setting myself a target and then hitting it. HowThese days, though, I judge a race by how well I ran, not just by where I finished. ExampleTake a 10 km road race I ran in Hà Nội last month: I came fourth in my age group, just outside the medals, but I knocked forty seconds off my best time. ResultAs a result, I crossed the line happier than the runner who won, because I knew I’d done my best. LimitationAdmittedly, a team final is a different story, because when three teammates are counting on me, the result is all I can think about. EvaluationEven so, I’m not afraid of losing to someone better, and if I had to choose, I’d take a personal best over a lucky win every time.

  • include an ‑ing subject, an ‑ing after a verb and an ‑ing after a preposition
  • put like + ‑ing and would like to in one answer to show the difference
  • use one Tier 2 chunk (a sore loser, learn to win and lose, take part in, as long as)
  • end your post with a question: Is anyone interested in …ing?
Suggested answers · 3 levels
● Core

To a partnerHi, I’m Nam. I love playing football, and I go running every morning. I’m good at running, but I’m not good at shooting. I don’t like losing, but I always try hard.

My postTraining partner wanted! Running alone is boring. I enjoy running in the morning, and I’m interested in training for a 10 km race. Is anyone free on Tuesday and Friday mornings?

●● Stretch

To a partnerI’m looking for someone to play badminton with twice a week. I’m quite good at smashing, but my footwork is slow, so I need a partner who can keep me moving. I’m fine with losing, as long as we both play hard and laugh about it afterwards.

My postBadminton partner wanted, Tuesdays and Thursdays after evening study. Playing the same person every week is the quickest way to improve. I enjoy long rallies more than winning easy points, and I’m not a sore loser, I promise! Is anyone interested in starting next week?

●●● Challenge

To a partnerI’d like to find someone to swim with, ideally a person who’s more serious than I am. I like swimming, but I’m hopeless at pushing myself when I’m alone, so I usually stop after twenty lengths. To be honest, I’m a bit competitive, which is why a partner who’s slightly faster would be perfect: chasing someone is the only thing that makes me try hard.

My postSwimming partner wanted for early mornings at the academy pool. Swimming before breakfast is hard to do alone, but easy with a friend waiting for you. I enjoy racing over short distances, and I’m keen on improving my turns. Speed doesn’t matter, as long as you turn up. Is anyone interested in taking part in the inter-faculty gala in March?

Step 6 / 6 · Recall

Alone, no notes

Active · alone⏱ 10 min
GoalTalk about sportspeople, winning and losing from memory, with your notes hidden.

Notes hidden? Look at the picture and talk about it in three sentences: who the player is, what he is doing and how top players feel about losing.

Compare with a model

This is Lionel Messi, the Argentinian footballer, playing for his national team. He’s running with the ball at his feet, probably looking for a teammate to pass to. Players at his level hate losing, but what makes them champions is learning from a defeat and coming back stronger in the next match.

The sport I’m best at is ________, but I’m hopeless at ________. I love ________ and I can’t stand ________. For me, winning is ________ because ________. ________ is the best way to ________. One sportsperson I’d like to meet is ________ because ________.
